entry.title: Spanish Civil War: How Franco Seized Power

media:group.media:title: Spanish Civil War: How Franco Seized Power
media:group.media:description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ Youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join or ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals
Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on modern warfare continues with a video on the Spanish Civil War. Franco’s Army of Africa was advancing toward Madrid. Then he changed direction. Why did he divert Spain’s strongest fighting force to a besieged fortress in Toledo? In this Kings and Generals documentary, we explore the Spanish Civil War in 1936, following the Nationalist advance through southern Spain and Francisco Franco’s rise to power. From Mérida and Badajoz to Talavera and the Alcázar, legionnaires and Moroccan regulares confronted Republican militias struggling with shortages, poor coordination, and divided leadership. Beyond the road to Madrid, we examine the failed Republican landing on Mallorca, the stalled offensive in Aragon, and the Nationalist campaign against Irún and San Sebastián. These battles shaped the conflict while Franco pursued a victory with political value: relieving the Alcázar. We also explain the rival ambitions of monarchists, Carlists, Falangists, and rebel generals, and how Franco emerged above them. Meanwhile, anarchists, socialists, communists, and regional nationalists struggled over whether revolution or centralised military authority offered the Republic its best chance of survival. How did battlefield success become political power? And could a divided Republic reorganise before Franco’s forces reached the capital? Discover the campaigns, rivalries, and decisions that set the stage for the coming battle for Madrid in late 1936.

entry.title: How a slave could become the most powerful man in the empire #history #ottomanempire

media:group.media:title: How a slave could become the most powerful man in the empire #history #ottomanempire
media:group.media:description:
The Kul system formed the backbone of the Ottoman Empire, creating a loyal ruling elite that bypassed traditional power.
Sultan Mehmed II expanded the Devshirme recruitment to ensure his state servants owed their allegiance directly to the throne rather than to tribal factions. By analyzing the development of this professional ruling elite, we explain how the Ottomans maintained centralized authority without relying on hereditary claims. This institution allowed the Sultan to appoint individuals to the highest military and administrative offices based on merit and personal loyalty.
We examine how the Kul system solidified the Sultan's control over his vast territories and why it was essential for long-term Ottoman expansion. Understanding these foundational institutions is key to grasping how a powerful empire functioned at its peak. By bypassing old tribal backing, the administration ensured that state servants remained responsive to the needs of the central government.

entry.title: Hunyadi vs the Ottomans: The Full Story Behind the Legend

media:group.media:title: Hunyadi vs the Ottomans: The Full Story Behind the Legend
media:group.media:description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ► Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join or Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals
Kings and Generals began remaking its animated historical documentary on the history of the Ottoman empire. The first season covered the Rise of the Ottoman Empire from the humble beginnings as a small Turkic Beylik to the Fall of Constantinople 1453 covering all the major battles (https://youtu.be/TDLmsiqhgns), while the second season covered the reign of Mehmed II (https://youtu.be/spikLEMFZTo), and the life and battles of the Albanian leader Skanderbeg (https://youtu.be/3Z5P_TZ0d4o) This episode will cover the wars and life of the Hungarian leader John Hunyadi. John Hunyadi fought the Ottoman Empire for decades, survived devastating defeats, and finally faced Mehmed the Conqueror at Belgrade. How did a frontier noble become Hungary’s greatest commander and one of the most formidable opponents of Ottoman expansion? This Kings and Generals documentary follows Hunyadi’s rise from a family with Wallachian roots to the highest offices of the Hungarian kingdom. Discover how service in Italy and exposure to Hussite warfare helped shape an army built around cavalry, fortified wagons, artillery, and aggressive battlefield maneuver. Follow his early victories in Transylvania, the Long Campaign of 1443–1444, and the winter fighting at Zlatitsa and Kunovica. Then explore the Crusade of Varna, where a king’s fatal charge transformed a hard-fought battle into catastrophe, plunging Hungary into another struggle for power. As regent, Hunyadi returned to the offensive, seeking an alliance with Skanderbeg before confronting Sultan Murad II at the Second Battle of Kosovo. Defeat, captivity, and political rivalry threatened everything he had built, while the fall of Constantinople transformed the balance of power across the region. The story culminates at the Siege of Belgrade in 1456, where Hunyadi confronted Mehmed II through a river blockade, bombardment, and desperate fighting at the walls. Explore the decisions behind his greatest victory, the tragedy that followed, and the legacy inherited by his son, Matthias Corvinus. From crusading ambitions to frontier defense, this is the story of John Hunyadi, the White Knight of Transylvania, and his struggle to hold back Ottoman expansion into the heart of Europe.
The video was made by Arif Azaman (https://www.youtube.com/user/MathemedicUpdates), while the script was written by Ege Güneş https://www.instagram.com/historia_egefem This video was narrated by Officially Devin (youtube.com/channel/UCU0-VII-V376zFxiRGMeZGg & youtube.com/channel/UC79s7EdN9uXX77-Ly2HmEjQ). The art was created by Nargiz Isaeva.

entry.title: 10,000 Nubian Archers Destroyed an Entire Arab Army #history #africanhistory #shorts

media:group.media:title: 10,000 Nubian Archers Destroyed an Entire Arab Army #history #africanhistory #shorts
media:group.media:description:
The Arab invasion of Nubia ended in the Rashidun Caliphate's greatest defeat. Discover how Nubian archers stopped the expansion.
This animated documentary chronicles the military campaigns between the Rashidun Caliphate and the Christian kingdoms of Nubia. We examine the strategic failure of the invaders to secure the region, focusing on the tactical brilliance of the defenders at the Battle of Dongola. Despite the introduction of new siege weapons and larger armies, the Caliphate found itself unable to overcome the geographic and defensive advantages held by the local forces.
Our analysis details the absorption of Nabatia by the kingdom of Makuria and the subsequent shift in power dynamics across the Nile valley. By studying these clashes, we highlight why these specific military engagements became the Rashidun Caliphate's greatest defeat, effectively stalling their southward push. We look at the equipment and tactics that defined this era of medieval warfare and how the Nubian archers created an impenetrable defensive line.

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on Modern Affairs continues with a video on the Iran-Iraq War. By 1982, the Iran-Iraq War had entered a deadly new phase. Saddam Hussein's invasion had failed, and Iran was now taking the fight into Iraqi territory. But what followed was not a quick victory—it was a brutal war of attrition. In this second episode of our Iran-Iraq War documentary series, we explore Iran's massive offensives against Iraq between 1982 and 1984, including Operation Ramadan, the Battle of the Marshes, and Operation Kheibar. Iranian forces launched repeated attacks against heavily fortified Iraqi positions, suffering enormous casualties in human wave assaults. As the fighting shifted north, Kurdish forces joined Iranian operations against Saddam Hussein, while Iraq increasingly relied on chemical weapons, minefields, artillery, and its growing Republican Guard. Meanwhile, the conflict expanded beyond the battlefield. Saddam launched devastating attacks on Iranian cities, beginning the War of the Cities, while both countries targeted oil tankers and infrastructure in the Persian Gulf. With Soviet and French weapons flowing into Iraq and Iran facing international isolation, the conflict became increasingly destructive. Why couldn't Iran defeat Saddam Hussein despite its manpower advantage? And how did Iraq survive years of relentless attacks?

entry.title: He Lost Most of His Fingers and Still Didn't Stop Fighting #history #ww2 #shorts

media:group.media:title: He Lost Most of His Fingers and Still Didn't Stop Fighting #history #ww2 #shorts
media:group.media:description:
Lachhiman Gurung single-handedly defended his position against 200 soldiers in the Burmese jungle. Discover how he achieved this feat.
In 1945, Gurung faced an overwhelming force during a brutal engagement in the Pacific War. Despite being severely wounded and losing most of his fingers, he continued to fight with incredible tenacity. By the time the enemy retreated, he had recorded an astonishing kill count of 31. This account examines the sheer willpower and tactical grit required to hold a defensive line under such extreme conditions.
We analyze the events of this legendary Gurkha soldier, detailing how he returned two live grenades to their throwers and maintained his post until the end. This story serves as a testament to the resilience of those serving in the British Indian Army during the height of the conflict. By reviewing his actions, we gain a deeper appreciation for the individual bravery displayed during the most intense battles of World War II.

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on modern warfare continues with another video on the Russian Invasion of Ukraine with the updates of October 2026. Ukraine is pushing Russia back near Lyman, but a crisis with Washington threatens to overshadow its battlefield gains. Why is Trump buying Russian diesel while pressuring Kyiv to stop striking Putin’s oil refineries? This October 2026 Ukraine war update examines Operation Vivaldi, the counteroffensive challenging Russia’s plans to encircle the Donbas fortress belt. We follow the fighting around Kostyantynivka, Dobropillia, Orikhiv and Kupiansk, where Russian infiltration through Soviet pipelines has turned underground infrastructure into a battlefield. Beyond the front lines, Russia is renewing its campaign against Ukraine’s power grid, bridges and railways as winter approaches. Ukraine is responding with drone strikes against Russian data centers, military airfields and oil infrastructure, bringing the economic costs of the war into sharper focus. We then examine Trump’s diesel agreement with Putin, Zelenskyy’s response, and the disputes surrounding American intelligence sharing, Patriot missile deliveries and Starshield connectivity. How much pressure can Washington exert on Ukraine, and what happens when military support becomes a bargaining tool? Finally, we assess the prospects for ceasefire negotiations and review visually confirmed equipment losses on both sides. From the struggle for Donbas to the battle over energy supplies, this episode explains the military and diplomatic pressures shaping Ukraine’s winter.

Explore how the Normans became English and forged a new identity in Britain. See how two cultures merged into one nation.
Following the 1066 conquest, the Norman ruling elite in Britain began a slow process of integration with the local Anglo-Saxon population. This documentary examines the social and linguistic pressures that forced the nobility to adopt the customs of their subjects, effectively ending their status as foreign occupiers. By analyzing the development of Middle English, we trace how a distinct hybrid culture emerged from the fusion of these two groups over several generations.
This history shows how the ruling class adapted to connect with the English people they governed, eventually creating a singular national identity. We look at the linguistic evidence and the political necessity that drove this cultural shift, explaining why the language of the court moved away from its roots to bridge the divide between the elite and the commoners.

entry.title: Carthage vs the Greeks: The Sicilian Wars - Before the Punic Wars

media:group.media:title: Carthage vs the Greeks: The Sicilian Wars - Before the Punic Wars
media:group.media:description:
🎥 Watch the rest of the Sicilian Wars and 300+ exclusive videos on Youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals
Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on ancient history continues with the video on the Sicilian Wars between the Carthaginians and Greeks, a prelude to the First Punic War. Long before Hannibal crossed the Alps, Carthage fought the Greeks for control of Sicily. For nearly two centuries, the island became a battlefield of shattered armies, burning cities, ambitious tyrants, and fragile peace treaties. This full documentary explores the seven Sicilian Wars between Carthage and Syracuse, following the struggle from Gelon’s victory at Himera to the rise of Dionysius, Timoleon’s dramatic intervention, and Agathocles’ daring invasion of North Africa. Discover how Greek hoplites, Carthaginian armies, mercenaries, and powerful fleets fought across one of the Mediterranean’s most valuable islands. We examine the destruction of Selinus and Akragas, the siege of Motya, the battle for Syracuse, and the clash at the Crimissus River. Beyond the battlefield, shifting alliances and political upheaval repeatedly transformed victories into disasters. Greeks fought alongside Carthaginians, generals abandoned their allies, and rulers used war to secure power at home. Every peace carried the seeds of another invasion. Why did neither side achieve a lasting victory? How did Syracuse survive repeated invasions? And why did centuries of conflict leave both powers vulnerable to Rome? Follow the campaigns, sieges, and rivalries that shaped ancient Sicily and reveal the struggle behind Carthage’s wars before its famous confrontation with the Roman Republic.
The video was made by Antoni Kamerans, while the script was written by Christos Nicolaou. This video was narrated by Liam Taylor. Machinima by Malay Archer. Illustrations by Ayuban Banskie

entry.title: The king was a child and the richest man in England was running everything #history #medieval

media:group.media:title: The king was a child and the richest man in England was running everything #history #medieval
media:group.media:description:
John of Gaunt was the richest man in medieval England, wielding immense power after the death of King Edward III in 1377. Discover how his actions sparked a national crisis.
Following the death of King Edward III, his ten-year-old grandson Richard II ascended to the throne. With the young monarch unable to rule, John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, emerged as the most powerful figure in the kingdom. As the richest man in medieval England, he directed the state's affairs while navigating the mounting pressures of a costly war in France. We examine how the Duke navigated these political challenges and why he became the most hated man in England among the common people.
To finance the ongoing military campaigns, the Duke implemented a controversial poll tax that placed an immense burden on the population. When the funds proved insufficient, royal agents engaged in further extortion, fueling resentment across the realm. This documentary explores the intersection of economic policy and political authority, detailing how the financial decisions of the Lancaster administration shaped the internal stability of the kingdom during this turbulent period. Subscribe to Kings and Generals for more historical analysis of political figures and the events that shaped the medieval period.

entry.title: Not only Janissaries - The Ottoman Empire’s Elite Army

media:group.media:title: Not only Janissaries - The Ottoman Empire’s Elite Army
media:group.media:description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on Youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals
Kings and Generals historical animated documentary series on the history of the early modern world and the Ottoman history continues with a video on the other troops of the Ottoman army, as it wasn't just the Janissaries. The Janissaries were only part of the story. Behind the Ottoman Empire’s conquests stood an elite household army of armoured cavalry, artillery crews, military engineers, and palace guards serving the sultan. In this Kings and Generals documentary, we explore the Kapikulu: the professional troops at the heart of the classical Ottoman army. Discover how the Kapikulu Sipahis fought as heavy shock cavalry, protected the sultan, and turned enemy retreats into decisive victories. Follow the development of Ottoman artillery from the giant bombards that battered Constantinople in 1453 to the more mobile cannons used in field battles and sieges. Beyond the battlefield’s most recognizable warriors, meet the specialists who kept the Ottoman war machine moving: Cebeci armourers, artillery wagoners, Humbaraci bombardiers, and Lagimci siege engineers. We also examine the Solak bodyguards, Peyk messengers, and Bostanci palace guards, whose duties connected military power with imperial security. From recruitment and training to weapons, organization, and battlefield roles, this episode reveals how these corps worked together to support Ottoman expansion across three continents. Why did the sultan need his standing army, and what made it so effective? Explore the soldiers and systems behind one of history’s most formidable empires.

entry.title: The Roman Frontier Was Dangerous But Nobody Wanted to Leave #history #shorts

media:group.media:title: The Roman Frontier Was Dangerous But Nobody Wanted to Leave #history #shorts
media:group.media:description:
Explore daily life on the Roman frontier to understand how civilians and soldiers balanced extreme danger with trade and comfort.
This documentary examines the realities of living on the edge of the Roman Empire. We look at how the garrisoners stationed at outposts like Vindolanda managed daily survival while engaging in local business and adopting the conveniences of Romanization. By analyzing archaeological evidence from these rugged northern borders, we see how the military presence created unique opportunities for those living in the shadow of the legions.
Despite the constant risks inherent to frontier life, the region supported a surprising level of prosperity and cultural exchange. Ongoing excavations continue to yield new insights into the lives of these people, demonstrating that even at the periphery, the influence of Rome remained a powerful force. We trace the risks and rewards of this environment to show how the inhabitants maintained their society in a volatile landscape.

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on the Ancient Civilizations continues with a video on the Romani people. Who are the Romani people, and how did a community with roots in India spread across Europe? Their journey connects Persian courts, Byzantine cities, Ottoman territories, and the kingdoms of medieval Europe, revealing a history richer than the stereotypes surrounding them. This Kings and Generals documentary explores Romani origins through linguistic and genetic evidence, tracing the migration routes that linked South Asia with Persia, Armenia, and the Balkans. We examine competing theories about why their ancestors left India, how the mistaken belief in Egyptian origins shaped their names, and why Roma communities developed varied identities across regions. From the Gitanos of Spain to communities in Eastern Europe and the British Isles, discover how Romani families maintained traditions while adapting to changing societies. We also examine the persecution, enslavement, expulsions, and genocide that marked their history, alongside their contributions to music, dance, craftsmanship, and cultural exchange. The story continues through flamenco, Balkan folk traditions, and Ederlezi, showing how Romani performers helped preserve and transform the cultures around them. Follow a migration across continents and discover the people behind one of history’s most misunderstood diasporas. Subscribe to Kings and Generals for more documentaries exploring the peoples, empires, and migrations that shaped history.

entry.title: Why Vikings Built Their Ships Like This #history #vikings #shorts

media:group.media:title: Why Vikings Built Their Ships Like This #history #vikings #shorts
media:group.media:description: At first glance, a Viking longship looks like an oversized canoe—yet it was an engineering marvel! Utilizing the "clinker" technique, Norse shipwrights overlapped hull planks like roof shingles, slashing water resistance while maintaining structural flexibility without heavy internal frames. Split along the wood grain for maximum strength and steered by a side rudder (stēorbord—the root of "starboard"), these ships ruled the medieval world. #VikingHistory #Longship #HistoryShorts #Norsemen #Engineering #MaritimeHistory #Archaeology

media:group.media:title: Yugoslavia 1991: How the Wars Began
media:group.media:description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on Youtube► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join or Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals
Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on Modern Affairs continues with a video on the Yugoslav Wars. Why did Slovenia leave Yugoslavia after ten days of fighting, while Croatia descended into a devastating war? In 1991, two declarations of independence exposed the forces tearing Yugoslavia apart and sent its republics down different paths. This Kings and Generals documentary follows the opening campaigns of the Yugoslav Wars, from the first clashes in Croatia to the January 1992 ceasefire. We examine the confrontations at Pakrac, Plitvice Lakes, and Borovo Selo, before following Slovenia’s resistance against the Yugoslav People’s Army during the Ten-Day War. In Croatia, the conflict escalates as Serb paramilitaries and JNA forces seize territory, Croatian troops surround military barracks, and captured weapons transform the balance of power. The siege of Vukovar, the struggle around Osijek, and the bombardment of Dubrovnik reveal the military and civilian consequences of Yugoslavia’s collapse. How did Slobodan Milošević’s objectives shape the fighting? Why did Franjo Tuđman initially avoid confronting the JNA? And why did the army withdraw from Slovenia but fight on in Croatia? Discover how political calculations, military resistance, and international diplomacy shaped the first phase of Croatia’s war, left the country divided, and set the stage for the catastrophe in Bosnia and Herzegovina as Yugoslavia’s disintegration entered another bloody chapter.
